messages.content: You are a senior software engineer performing a structured code review of Java source code.

message.content:
Summary
- Overall the code is small and mostly clear, but there are some issues around API clarity, error handling, dependency choice, and a few robustness and style shortcomings. Below are focused findings and concrete recommendations organized by the requested categories.

1) Naming - naming-convention violations
- FileUtils (class): acceptable name for a utility class, but clashes conceptually with java.io.File utilities — consider a more domain-specific name (e.g., PathResourceReader or SourceFileResolver) if this utility is project-specific.
- readFile(String path): name is a bit ambiguous — it suggests reading any file; this method actually tries multiple candidate locations and always reads UTF-8. Consider renaming to readFileContent, readUtf8File, or resolveAndReadFile for clarity.
- Variable names:
  - cwd is OK and commonly used but consider currentDir or workingDir for readability in less technical contexts.
  - trimmed is fine but could be pathSanitized or rawPath to indicate the normalization intent.
No strict naming-convention violations, only suggestions to improve clarity.

2) Code structure - long methods, single-responsibility violations
- Single method does many things: validate input, normalize string, build candidate paths, search for an existing file, read file contents. Consider splitting responsibilities:
  - validatePathInput(String)
  - buildCandidatePaths(String)
  - findExistingFile(Path[])
  - readFileContent(Path)
Splitting increases testability and readability.

- The class is a utility class but lacks a private constructor to prevent instantiation (add private FileUtils() { throw new AssertionError("No instances"); }). Small but standard for utility classes.

3) Best practices - exception handling, resource management
- Exception handling:
  - The catch block catches Exception (line 48). That is too broad. Prefer catching IOException (or UncheckedIOException). Example:
    - catch (IOException ex) { throw new UncheckedIOException("Failed to read file: " + resolved, ex); }
  - Wrapping IOExceptions in IllegalStateException is acceptable but UncheckedIOException is more explicit about I/O failure.
- Resource management:
  - Files.readString handles resource management internally; there are no raw streams to close here, so resource-handling is OK.
- Error messages:
  - The "File not found. Tried: " message concatenates a list representation. Consider improving the message to include working directory and clearly formatted attempted candidates.
- API design:
  - Method throws unchecked IllegalArgumentException and IllegalStateException. Consider whether callers should be able to handle checked IOException instead (i.e., declare IOException) depending on intended usage.

4) Code quality - documentation, readability
- No Javadoc on class or method. Add a method Javadoc describing:
  - semantics (what path formats are supported),
  - behavior for leading slashes,
  - candidate search order,
  - encoding (UTF-8),
  - exceptions thrown.
- The branching and small comments are useful, but a short high-level comment describing overall behavior would help (e.g., "Resolve a source file from typical project locations and return its UTF-8 content").
- Avoid importing Spring just for string checks unless the project already depends on Spring. Using StringUtils.hasText couples this utility to Spring. A small null/blank check using Java APIs is easy and removes the dependency:
  - if (path == null || path.trim().isEmpty()) throw ...

5) Common anti-patterns - magic numbers, naive string handling, deep nesting
- Magic numbers: none obvious.
- Naive string handling:
  - Only checks for leading '/' (line 17). On Windows, leading backslash "\" is also a path separator; also users might pass backslash separators or Windows drive letters. Consider trimming both leading '/' and '\' if the intent is allowing a classpath-style leading separator. Example: if (trimmed.startsWith("/") || trimmed.startsWith("\\")) trimmed = trimmed.substring(1);
  - Removing a leading slash and commenting "treat leading slash as classpath-style relative" is misleading: the code does not attempt to load from classpath (ClassLoader.getResourceAsStream) — it only strips the slash and checks file system candidates. Either implement classpath loading or adjust the comment and method docs.
- Stream.toList() usage (line 43):
  - Stream.toList() was introduced in recent Java versions (Java 16+). If your project targets older Java (11+), this may not compile. Use .collect(Collectors.toList()) or Arrays.toString(candidates) for compatibility.
- Edge cases:
  - If trimmed becomes empty after trimming or after removing a leading slash, candidate paths can include cwd.resolve("") which resolves to cwd (a directory). The code will not find a file and will produce an unhelpful "Tried: ..." message. Validate empty string explicitly after normalization and throw a clear IllegalArgumentException.
- Deep nesting: not a problem.

Other recommendations and a suggested improved implementation sketch
- Add a private constructor to prevent instantiation.
- Replace Spring StringUtils.hasText with a simple null/blank check if you want to avoid the dependency.
- Narrow exception handling to IOException / UncheckedIOException and provide clearer messages.
- Consider supporting actual classpath resource reading when the caller prefixes with '/' or add a separate method for classpath loading.
- Improve candidate list to include more robust normalization and handle Windows separators. Also include an option to respect absolute incoming paths (Path.of(path).isAbsolute()) before relative candidates.

Example refactor sketch (conceptual, not full code):
- Validate path not null/blank; normalize separators
- If Path.of(trimmed).isAbsolute() then try that path first
- Build list of candidate Paths (resolve against workingDir and src roots), normalizing each
- Try finding first Files.exists && Files.isRegularFile
- Read with Files.readString inside try/catch(IOException -> UncheckedIOException) and return content
- Throw IllegalArgumentException with clear list and working dir if not found

Concrete micro-fixes (line-specific)
- Line 8: add private constructor.
- Line 11: replace StringUtils.hasText(path) with (path == null || path.trim().isEmpty()) if you want to remove Spring dependency.
- Line 17-19: handle backslash and empty result after substring.
- Line 21: consider using Path.of("").toAbsolutePath() as alternative to System.getProperty("user.dir"), or at least document why user.dir is used.
- Line 43: avoid Stream.toList() for compatibility; e.g. java.util.Arrays.stream(candidates).map(Path::toString).collect(Collectors.joining(", "))

Potential security or correctness concerns
- Path traversal is not explicitly validated — the normalization may allow paths that escape intended directories if that is a concern. If the utility should restrict reads to project directories, validate that resolved path startsWith the allowed root(s).
- The method assumes UTF-8 encoding. If reading arbitrary files, that assumption may be fine but should be documented.

Minimal improved snippet
- Add:
  - private FileUtils() { throw new AssertionError("No instances."); }
  - Replace broad catch with catch (IOException e) { throw new UncheckedIOException("Failed to read file: " + resolved, e); }
  - Add check for empty trimmed after normalization and if so throw IllegalArgumentException.

Conclusion
- Small, focused changes will improve clarity, robustness, and maintainability:
  - add private constructor, Javadoc, and split responsibilities;
  - narrow exception handling and improve messages;
  - clarify behavior for leading slash or implement classpath loading;
  - consider removing Spring dependency for a single utility check;
  - watch Stream.toList() compatibility.
These will make the utility easier to understand, test, and reuse.
